title: Finn and the Hiccuping Dragon
markdown:
Once upon a time, in the warm cozy Mossymoon Mountains, lived a little wizard called Finn. Finn loved magic. He loved making little spells go fizz-pop and twinkle-shoo. He made lights dance on his fingers. He made yellow flowers float like tiny balloons. And oh, Finn loved snacks. Sunshine berries that tasted like happy giggles. Cloud bread, softer than a bunny’s ear, tasting of sweet dreams. But sometimes, when Finn ate his yummy supper, he thought it would be even yummier with a friend. He wished for someone to share his sunshine berries. He imagined a big sandwich of cloud bread, cut in half. One half for him. One half for a friend.

Every day, Finn gathered the juiciest sunshine berries, round and rosy, smelling like warm days. He found the fluffiest cloud bread he could, so light it almost floated away. He spread his favourite checkered blanket, squares of blue and yellow, on the softest mossy path in the mountains. A peaceful path, winding between cloud-pines whose branches drooped like soft green curtains. The air smelled of flowers and moss. Warm as a hug. A place for a quiet supper, where you could hear little rustles.

Until one day: sniffle-snuffle. Not water. A tiny sniffle-snuffle. Finn stopped spreading his blanket. He tilted his head. His wizard hat, a little too big, nearly slipped over his bright wondering eyes. Sniffle-snuffle. Behind a big round mossy stone that looked like a sleeping bear. Finn tiptoed closer. Wizard boots, squish-squish on the springy ground. Each step like a soft pillow.

Because of that, Finn peeked around the mossy stone. A little dragon. Not a big roaring one. About the size of a fluffy kitten, no bigger than Finn’s favourite cuddly toy. Scales green as emeralds, sparkling like little green stars. Wings like delicate dragonfly wings, shimmery and see-through, fluttering just a little. Big round eyes like bright pebbles. A tiny nose that twitched. And it was definitely doing the sniffle-snuffle. Tears like tiny sparkly drops rolling down its cheeks.

Finn remembered his mama telling him to be kind and to share smiles. He whispered, as soft as a butterfly’s wing.

“Hello there, little one. Are you all right? Why are you sniffing and snuffling?”

The dragon jumped a little, sparkly wings giving a quick flutter, then a tiny wobbly smile.

“Oh. Hello,” it squeaked, and tried to bow. It was very hard for a little dragon to bow properly. Its head wobbled like jelly on a plate. “My name is Flicker. I was hoping… could I watch you eat your supper? If that’s okay?” Flicker looked down at his little dragon claws, a bit embarrassed.

Finn’s face lit up brighter than any spell he had ever cast. A friend. For supper.

“Watch? Oh, you don’t have to just watch, Flicker. You can share my supper.” Already pulling out the cloud bread. He carefully broke off a big piece.

Because of that, Finn sat on his checkered blanket and offered Flicker a piece of cloud bread. Flicker took it very carefully with his dragon claws, making sure not to scratch the blanket. He nibbled. He chewed, trying to be quiet and polite. Then he ate a big sweet sunshine berry. Juicy. Delightful. Bursting with sunny flavour. Flicker was so excited about the berry that he let out a little unexpected hiccup. With the hiccup came a tiny puff of smoke, a little grey whisper that tickled Finn’s nose.

Finn did not jump. He did not flinch. He giggled, a giggle like little bells.

“That was a funny little puff. It tickled my nose.”

Flicker looked surprised, then smiled, and giggled too, a little puff of smoke with each giggle.

“Oh dear,” Flicker whispered, nose twitching. “My mama said dragons shouldn’t puff smoke when they eat. It’s not right.”

Finn patted the ground next to him, making space.

“It’s okay. It just means you really, really liked the berry. It’s a yummy berry. Here, try another. Maybe the juicy one.”

He handed Flicker another big sunshiny sunshine berry, glistening with sweet juice.

And so Flicker and Finn munched happily on more sunshine berries and cloud bread. Flicker tried really hard not to hiccup smoke, but sometimes a tiny puff escaped when he was very happy, and Finn would just laugh. They talked about the sparkly spells Finn liked to make. Flicker told Finn how he loved to watch the butterflies, wings like colourful silk. Finn found out that Flicker’s mama taught him to be polite by practising “Thank you ever so much” and “May I please have another” to the wind.

Until finally, as moonbeams twinkled through the cloud-pine leaves and made dancing patterns on Finn’s checkered blanket, they finished their supper. Flicker felt a little sleepy from all the yummy food and all the polite talking and giggling. He nudged Finn’s arm. Finn smiled a big warm smile. He pet Flicker’s green scales. Warm and smooth, like pretty stones. Flicker snuggled close, right on the soft moss. Night crickets. Still air. The mossy ground like a soft bed.

Ever since then, Finn and Flicker often shared suppers under the twinkling stars in the Mossymoon Mountains. Sunshine berries. Cloud bread. Happy giggles that sometimes, just sometimes, had a tiny puff of smoke attached. Finn spread the blue-and-yellow blanket as he always had. Now there were two halves of cloud bread, and two sets of crumbs, and a little grey whisper that meant the berries had been exactly right.
